Which release produced a normalizer signature

Source: R/signature.R
np_signature_history.Rd

np_normalize_signature() returns an opaque value, which is what makes it a good fingerprint and a poor label: it says that two artifacts disagree, never which is newer. This dates every signature the package has published, so a script writing a provenance header can stamp the release beside the signature instead of a person looking it up in NEWS.md.

Usage

np_signature_history(signature = NULL)

Arguments

signature

Optionally one or more signature strings to look up. A value that is not listed returns no rows — it is not an error, and it is not the same as a listed row with an NA version.

Value

A data frame of signature, package, version and summary, in publication order. version is the release that introduced the signature; a later release that reports the same value unchanged is named in summary rather than given a row of its own, so one signature is one row and the column stays usable for comparison.

Details

The three oldest rows are npmatch's, from before the normalizer moved into this package. They are listed so that an unrecognized value can be told from a recognized pre-split one; their npmatch version was never recorded, so version is NA and summary says where the value is cited.

A signature does not determine a release

A release that changes no rule reports its predecessor's value: 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 both report v1-3e7b9f9d59bbb19e. So this answers which release produced this value — meaning the earliest that could have — and not which release is installed. A stamped artifact wants both: the signature, so a reader can tell whether its keys are comparable with theirs, and utils::packageVersion() at build time, so they can tell what was running. Neither determines the other, and a header carrying only one of them invites the reader to infer the other.

See also

np_normalize_signature()

Examples

np_signature_history(np_normalize_signature())
#>             signature     package version
#> 1 v1-5e901add4a04a5d6 npnormalize   0.1.8
#>                                                                                               summary
#> 1 the join stops closing up a lone compass letter (#16); 0.1.9 reports it too, having changed no rule

# the whole history, oldest first
np_signature_history()[, c("signature", "package", "version")]
#>              signature     package version
#> 1  v1-421e1e2a6afb024e     npmatch    <NA>
#> 2  v1-6dcb298522cc5118     npmatch    <NA>
#> 3  v1-b42811fe6601afe6     npmatch    <NA>
#> 4  v1-3e7b9f9d59bbb19e npnormalize   0.1.0
#> 5  v1-6d90b52d8b781673 npnormalize   0.1.2
#> 6  v1-592912060053c4c3 npnormalize   0.1.3
#> 7  v1-1179714ce1e9d31f npnormalize   0.1.4
#> 8  v1-533f186c123357cf npnormalize   0.1.5
#> 9  v1-d49b18cc81ab79fb npnormalize   0.1.6
#> 10 v1-59c6e84c5f38e9f5 npnormalize   0.1.7
#> 11 v1-5e901add4a04a5d6 npnormalize   0.1.8
